correctness.rationale: For each unit direction zeta, the analytic shadow has coefficients a_n zeta^n+b_n conjugate(zeta)^n and exactly reproduces f(r zeta) on the real radius. Weighted radial orthogonality gives its exact A^2_alpha norm. The coefficient bound |u+v|^2<=2(|u|^2+|v|^2), together with beta_0=1, yields the center defect 2||f||^2-|f(0)|^2. The verified analytic Andreev inequality then gives the ray estimate, and the same shadow at negative radius gives the diameter estimate.

value.rationale: The fresh paper obtains its strongest Hilbert-space constant only after imposing f(0)=0. The accepted theorem removes that restriction, retains the exact center energy, and exposes directional cancellation between analytic and coanalytic modes. It therefore extends the improved diameter bound to every harmonic Bergman function for alpha>=0 and gives a strictly more informative ray quantity than a routine constant subtraction.
